properties.statement:
set_verification_status SILENTLY DELETED `last_run_at` WHEN THE OPTIONAL PARAMETER WAS OMITTED — data loss from the most ordinary act there is. FIXED 2026-08-09.

Filed by dev_storyflow 2026-08-08 and RE-FILED after retesting on 0.26.1, both times on a throwaway node created for the purpose and never on one whose timestamp anyone depended on. One variable: same node, same status, parameter omitted, key GONE. The key was REMOVED rather than set to null, so a wiped check was byte-identical to one that had never run.

CONFIRMED IN THE SOURCE HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE REPORT: verify.rs copied every existing property EXCEPT `status` and `last_run_at`, so an omitted `last_run_at` was excluded from the copy and never re-set.

WHY THE DIRECTION WAS THE BAD ONE, and this is their argument, not a restatement: it fires from marking a check `failing` after a regression — which erases the evidence it ever ran — and it fails toward `never_run`, precisely the field a later session greps for unproven work. It was invisible at the call site because the response is success-shaped and dominated by a long `name`.

AND IT BROKE A CONVENTION THIS CODEBASE STATES ELSEWHERE AS A PRINCIPLE, which is the cheapest thing to point at: set_interface_spec promises 'omitting one LEAVES IT ALONE', set_decision_status 'Every other property is preserved', set_epoch_status 'Everything else about the epoch is preserved'. This function's own first line said 'preserving its other properties' and then null-wrote one of them. One tool departing from a convention the others state is worse than no convention, because a caller who has read any sibling reasonably assumes it.

THE FIX: `last_run_at` is replaced only when the caller supplies one. Clearing a run time is therefore not expressible by omission, and should not be — erasing evidence is a deliberate act and deserves a deliberate call. PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL: restoring the old one-line condition fails the new test on exactly the data-loss assertion. The test also pins the other direction (an explicit timestamp still overwrites), because a fix that made the parameter inert would be the same bug pointing the other way.

⚠️ WORTH CARRYING TO THE FLEET: they upgraded to 0.26.1 partly on the understanding that filed bugs were fixed, and said so — several were, this one was not, and a reader skimming 'we upgraded, bugs fixed' would reasonably have assumed otherwise. The retest is what caught it.
properties.value: {"reported":"dev_storyflow 2026-08-08, re-filed after 0.26.1 retest 2026-08-09","root_cause":"verify.rs copied all properties except status and last_run_at, so an omitted last_run_at was dropped","fix":"last_run_at replaced only when supplied","negative_control":"old condition restored -> new test fails on the data-loss assertion","siblings_documenting_the_opposite":"set_interface_spec, set_decision_status, set_epoch_status"}
